arxiv-2305-08873.title: Thermodynamic variational relation
arxiv-2305-08873.creator: Domingos S. P. Salazar
arxiv-2305-08873.description: Abstract In systems far from equilibrium, the statistics of observables are connected to entropy production, leading to the Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation (TUR). However, the derivation of TURs often involves constraining the parity of observables, such as considering asymmetric currents, making it unsuitable for the general case.

arxiv-2306-00467.title: Efficient VQE Approach for Accurate Simulations on the Kagome Lattice
arxiv-2306-00467.creator: Jyothikamalesh S, Kaarnika A, Dr.Mohankumar.M, Sanjay Vishwakarma, Srinjoy Ganguly, Yuvaraj P
arxiv-2306-00467.description: Abstract The Kagome lattice, a captivating lattice structure composed of interconnected triangles with frustrated magnetic properties, has garnered considerable interest in condensed matter physics, quantum magnetism, and quantum computing.The Ansatz optimization provided in this study along with extensive research on optimisation technique results us with high accuracy.

arxiv-2307-02352.title: Optimal damping of vibrating systems: dependence on initial conditions Journal: Journal of Sound and Vibration
arxiv-2307-02352.creator: K. Lelas, I. Nakić
arxiv-2307-02352.description: Abstract Common criteria used for measuring performance of vibrating systems have one thing in common: they do not depend on initial conditions of the system. In some cases it is assumed that the system has zero initial conditions, or some kind of averaging is used to get rid of initial conditions.

arxiv-2308-04663.title: Classification of lung cancer subtypes on CT images with synthetic pathological priors
arxiv-2308-04663.creator: Wentao Zhu, Yuan Jin, Gege Ma, Geng Chen, Jan Egger, Shaoting Zhang, Dimitris N. Metaxas
arxiv-2308-04663.description: Abstract The accurate diagnosis on pathological subtypes for lung cancer is of significant importance for the follow-up treatments and prognosis managements. In this paper, we propose self-generating hybrid feature network (SGHF-Net) for accurately classifying lung cancer subtypes on computed tomography (CT) images.

arxiv-2311-14772.title: Trainwreck: A damaging adversarial attack on image classifiers
arxiv-2311-14772.creator: Jan Zahálka
arxiv-2311-14772.description: Abstract Adversarial attacks are an important security concern for computer vision (CV). As CV models are becoming increasingly valuable assets in applied practice, disrupting them is emerging as a form of economic sabotage. This paper opens up the exploration of damaging adversarial attacks (DAAs) that seek to damage target CV models.

arxiv-2312-04187.title: Enumerating Complexity Revisited
arxiv-2312-04187.creator: Alexander Shekhovtsov, Georgii Zakharov
arxiv-2312-04187.description: Abstract Abstract Consider a subset of positive integers S . In this paper, we reduce the upper bound on the length of a minimum program that enumerates S in terms of the probability of S being enumerated by a random program. So far, the best-known upper bound was given by Solovay.

arxiv-2402-09236.title: Learning Interpretable Concepts: Unifying Causal Representation Learning and Foundation Models
arxiv-2402-09236.creator: Goutham Rajendran ∗, Simon Buchholz, Bryon Aragam, Bernhard Schölkopf, Pradeep Ravikumar
arxiv-2402-09236.description: Abstract To build intelligent machine learning systems, there are two broad approaches. One approach is to build inherently interpretable models, as endeavored by the growing field of causal representation learning. The other approach is to build highly-performant foundation models and then invest efforts into understanding how they work.

pmc-11319464.title: Synchronized crystallization in tin-lead perovskite solar cells
pmc-11319464.creator: Yao Zhang, Chunyan Li, Haiyan Zhao, Zhongxun Yu, Xiaoan Tang, Jixiang Zhang, Zhenhua Chen, Jianrong Zeng, Peng Zhang, Liyuan Han, Han Chen
pmc-11319464.description: Tin-lead halide perovskites with a bandgap near 1.2 electron-volt hold great promise for thin-film photovoltaics. However, the film quality of solution-processed Sn-Pb perovskites is compromised by the asynchronous crystallization behavior between Sn and Pb components, where the crystallization of Sn-based perovskites tends to occur faster than that of Pb.

pmc-11394320.title: Importance of Transcript Variants in Transcriptome Analyses
pmc-11394320.creator: Kevin Vo, Yashica Sharma, Anohita Paul, Ryan Mohamadi, Amelia Mohamadi, Patrick E Fields, M A Karim Rumi, Subramaniam Malarkannan, Maurizio Romano
pmc-11394320.description: RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) has become a widely adopted technique for studying gene expression. However, conventional RNA-Seq analyses rely on gene expression (GE) values that aggregate all the transcripts produced under a single gene identifier, overlooking the complexity of transcript variants arising from different transcription start sites or alternative splicing.

pmc-11478316.title: Systematic Comparison of Extract Clean-Up with Currently Used Sorbents for Dispersive Solid-Phase Extraction
pmc-11478316.creator: Michelle Peter, Christoph Müller, Julia Martín, Esteban Alonso
pmc-11478316.description: Dispersive solid-phase extraction (dSPE) is a crucial step for multiresidue analysis used to remove matrix components from extracts. This purification prevents contamination of instrumental equipment and improves method selectivity, sensitivity, and reproducibility. Therefore, a clean-up step is recommended, but an over-purified extract can lead to analyte loss due to adsorption to the sorbent.

pmc-11512265.title: GPCR Inhibitors Have Antiviral Properties against JC Polyomavirus Infection
pmc-11512265.creator: Amanda L Sandberg, Avery C S Bond, Lucas J Bennett, Sophie E Craig, David P Winski, Lara C Kirkby, Abby R Kraemer, Kristina G Kelly, Samuel T Hess, Melissa S Maginnis, Ronald N Harty
pmc-11512265.description: JC polyomavirus (JCPyV) infects the majority of the population and initially establishes a persistent but asymptomatic infection of the kidneys. In healthy individuals, the infection remains controlled by the host immune system, but for individuals experiencing prolonged immunosuppression, the infection can reactivate and spread to the brain, where it causes progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), which is a fatal neurodegenerative disease.

pmc-12581442.title: Genomic signatures of subterranean lifestyle and ecological adaptation in Myospalax
pmc-12581442.creator: Na Wan, Jiaqi Chen, Muli Jiang, Mengzhuo Wu, Haolin Li, Mozhi Wen, Wei Shen, Xiaolong Liang, Xiaojie Yang, Yijing Liu, Yige Gao, Eviatar Nevo, Kexin Li
pmc-12581442.description: BackgroundMammals exhibit diverse adaptations to varied habitats, yet the genomic mechanisms underlying these transitions remain incompletely understood. Here, we present a comparative genomic, epigenomic, and three-dimensional chromatin analysis of two closely related zokor species, Myospalax aspalax and Myospalax psilurus, which inhabit arid and humid subterranean environments, respectively.

pmc-12655914.title: An Edge-Enabled Lightweight LSTM for the Temperature Prediction of Electrical Joints in Low-Voltage Distribution Cabinets
pmc-12655914.creator: Yuan Gui, Chengdong Yin, Ruoxi Liu, Hanqi Dai, Longfei He, Jiawei Zhao, Quanji Ma, Chongshan Zhong
pmc-12655914.description: Joint overheating in low-voltage distribution cabinets presents a major safety risk, often leading to insulation failure, accelerated aging, and even fires. Conventional threshold-based inspection methods are limited in detecting early temperature evolution and lack predictive capabilities. To address this, a short-term temperature prediction method for electrical joints based on deep learning is proposed.

pmc-12888680.title: Subtype-specific health and economic impact of delayed breast cancer diagnosis during the early COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium: a Markov model analysis
pmc-12888680.creator: Yasmine Khan, Nick Verhaeghe, Chris Monten, Katrien Vanthomme, Sylvie Gadeyne, Brecht Devleesschauwer, Freija Verdoodt, Hanna M Peacock, Delphine De Smedt
pmc-12888680.description: BackgroundDuring the first COVID-19 wave, breast cancer diagnoses declined sharply worldwide due to suspended screening programmes and delayed care-seeking driven by fear of infection. In Belgium, organized screening programmes were halted from March to June 2020, leaving 135 invasive breast cancers undiagnosed.

pmc-13259429.title: Finite-Element Analysis of the Quasi-Static Response of Concrete Specimens Containing Polymeric Self-Healing Microcapsules
pmc-13259429.creator: Todor Zhelyazov
pmc-13259429.description: Healing agent encapsulated in polymeric microcapsules has proven its ability to seal surface and internal cracks. Focused on mitigating the negative impact of capsules on the properties of fresh cement paste and hardened cementitious matrix, uncertainties in self-healing triggering, and poor control of the released quantity, researchers report technological improvements in predominantly experimental studies.

pmc-13535400.title: 28 Real-World Treatment Patterns, Healthcare Resource Utilization (HCRU) And Costs in First-Line (1L) Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma (aRCC) in the US
pmc-13535400.creator: Neil Shah, Ching-Yu Wang, Pratik Rane, Wei Gao, Esteban Lemus Wirtz, Tina Long, Julia Koloskova, Robert Motzer
pmc-13535400.description: BackgroundAdvances in tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) and immuno-oncology (IO) therapies have reshaped the aRCC treatment landscape, necessitating an updated understanding of real-world treatment patterns, HCRU, and costs.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using Optum’s deidentified Clinformatics® Data Mart Database (2019-2024).

pmc-13642403.title: Digitalisierung und Künstliche Intelligenz in der Intensiv- und Notfallmedizin
pmc-13642403.creator: Leo Benning, Markus Haar, Anna Haftenberger, Dario Antweiler, Oliver Steidle, Ralf Möller, Robert Simon Schiff, Sebastian Wolfrum, Mattis Hartwig, Marek Seitz, Georg Widhalm, Sabine Wingen, Hans-Jörg Busch, Guido Michels
pmc-13642403.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In diesem Impulspapier legt die Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internistische Intensiv- und Notfallmedizin e. (DGIIN) grundlegende Prinzipien für die zielgerichtete Einführung von Digitalisierung und künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) in der Notfall- und Intensivmedizin dar. Diese Einführung erfordert eine gezielte Qualifizierung aller an der Patientenversorgung beteiligten Berufsgruppen, um technologische Grundlagen, Unsicherheiten, regulatorische Rahmenbedingungen sowie Möglichkeiten und Grenzen medizinischer Anwendungsszenarien in diesen Versorgungsbereichen beurteilen zu können.
